Let $A_1 A_2 A_3 \ldots A_{11}$ be an $11$-sided non-convex simple polygon with the following properties:

\begin{itemize}
\item For every integer $2 \le i \le 10$,  the area of $\triangle A_i A_{1} A_{i+1}$  is equal to $1$.
\item For every integer $2 \le i \le 10$, $\cos(\angle A_i A_{1} A_{i+1}) = \frac{12}{13}$.
\item The perimeter of the $11$-gon $A_1 A_2 A_3 \dots A_{11}$  is equal to $20$.
\end{itemize}

Then $A_1 A_2 + A_1 A_{11} = \frac{m \sqrt{n} - p}{q}$ where $m, n, p$, and $q$ are positive integers, $n$ is not divisible by the square of any prime, and no prime divides all of $m, p$, and $q$. Find $m + n + p + q$.

source_statement: Suppose $D$, $E$ are points on the sides $AB$, $AC$, respectively, of a triangle $ABC$, and the following are known: $AB = 6$, $AC = 9$, $AD = 4$, $AE = 6$. Suppose, furthermore, the circum-circle of the triangle $ADE$ intersects the side $BC$ at two points $F$, $G$ and the points $B$, $F$, $G$, $C$ are lined up in this order. If the point of intersection of the lines $DF$ and $EG$ lies on the circum-circle of the triangle $ABC$, find the value of $\frac{FG}{BC}$. Here $XY$ denotes the length of the line segment $XY$ as well.

cause: cx>0 guard excludes the valid AB>AC branch
evidence_detail: Independent construction gives AB≈7.0906225924=(81+9*sqrt(13))/16, AC≈3.03437741, angle A=2π/3, and DE=DI=EI=1 with AB>AC. In the DSL gauge C=(cx,cy), this valid branch has cx=-(AC)/2<0, but the DSL requires AssumeGt(cx,0). Thus no_solution is caused by an overrestrictive DSL guard.
